info.title: with-secrets authority administration API
info.description: The administration API of the with-secrets authority on the Windows host service's loopback port (same origin as the administration web application). JSON only. A browser session is READ-ONLY (an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie plus a secret given once, in service memory only). Every administrative change needs its own fresh passkey authorization; the narrow exception is Deny request in Approvals, which releases no secrets. Approve once uses its own fresh request-bound WebAuthn challenge and assertion; it records a once-only grant that the run it approves uses up, and it is not an administrative authorization, bound to the operation and its parameters, single use and time limited. There is no CORS. Changes within v1 are additive; a breaking change is a new major version. Another version number (/api/v2/...) is answered with 400 and the problem code unsupported-api-version listing supportedVersions; an unknown path under /api is 404 route-not-found; /api never falls through to the web application. Every response carries X-Api-Version; a request may carry it too (X-Api-Version: 1) and another value is refused with unsupported-api-version. No answer contains a secret value, a credential, a private key or recovery material.

sessionCookie.name: ws_session
sessionCookie.description: A read-only browser session (admin or approval scope; HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path /api/v1). The value is bound to the service port. Alone it is not enough: the request must also carry the session's own secret (antiForgery).

browserCookie.name: ws_pre
browserCookie.description: The browser's pre-session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path /api/v1), made by POST /browser; with it, the anti-forgery value of POST /browser.

antiForgery.name: X-Admin-Token
antiForgery.description: A secret given once, in the answer that made the cookie it belongs to: POST /browser (before a session) or POST /session/claim (the session). Kept in the page, never in a cookie; the page's origin (with its port) is what keeps it from other programs that are sent the cookies.

type.description: A URI naming the kind of problem (urn:with-secrets:problem:CODE).

detail.description: One safe sentence. Never a secret, a credential, a key or an internal detail.

reuseMaxMinutes.description: The longest time a grant may be made for.

baseUrl.description: The address of the pages, or null for http://localhost.

port.description: The port the pages listen on; 0 picks a free one.

timeoutMinutes.description: How long the program waits for an answer on a page.

config.description: The instance's configuration as a JSON object on one line. Use the provider's sealing endpoint for credentials.

admin.description: Deprecated display alias for admin-scope sessions; use identity and scope.

identity.description: The trusted enrolled passkey identity that signed in.

antiForgery.description: Keep this in the page (not in a cookie) and send it as the X-Admin-Token header with every request. It is given once, here, and never again.
The session's own secret, given once, here. Send it as the X-Admin-Token header with every request: the session cookie alone is not enough.

link.description: The one-use passkey page to open. The tap there starts the session.

count.description: The most supersedes from another address seen within one watch window.

firstAddress.description: The address of the older connection when the warning was first recorded.

lastAddress.description: The address of the newest connection that superseded another.

CopyWarning.description: A warning (never a decision) that this machine's identity may have been copied: its connection was repeatedly superseded by a connection from a different address.

secretNames.description: The NAMES of the secrets the grant covers (never a value).

usage.description: reusable, or once (a grant that the one run it approved uses up).

replaces.description: The id of the used once-only grant this grant was made from.

verified.description: The grant seal verifies and the signing passkey is still authorized.

metadata.description: Names and fingerprints the host signed with the event (secret names, key name, reuse minutes, variable mapping, .env files, file fingerprints). Read-only data, never values.
Credential roles and identities recorded with the change.

authorityKey.description: The public fingerprint of the authority key in use.

id.description: Carry this in the `authorization` member of the one mutation it was made for.

link.description: The one-use passkey page to open (while pending). The tap there is the authorization.

sentence.description: Exactly what the passkey signs: show it to the person.

lifetimeSeconds.description: How long a verified authorization may wait for its mutation.

payload.description: Service-generated WebAuthn request data; the service retains the operation, nonce, origin and RP ID context.

outcome.description: applied: the service made the change when the tap was verified. started: the operation's own passkey pages continue at `link`. failed: the tap was good but the change was refused or could not be made (see `code` and `detail`); nothing was changed.

invitationGone.description: True when a new invitation's bundle was already given (or held for 5 minutes without being collected): it is never given again.

AuthorizationRequest.description: The operation and every parameter that the passkey will sign. The mutation that follows must repeat exactly these.

id.description: The invitation's identifier (not secret on its own: it is useless without the pairing code, which is never listed).

machine.description: The fingerprint of the machine that used it, once consumed.

bundle.description: The credential bundle: address, identifier and pairing code. Shown ONCE, in this answer. It is not stored in readable form, not logged and cannot be fetched again; give it to the new machine's pairing command (hidden prompt, an environment variable or, preferably, a secret file).

outcome.description: applied: done (the service made the change when the tap was verified). started: the first passkey page of an operation with pages of its own is at `link`. already-applied and already-started: a retry for an authorization that was already answered; nothing was applied again.
